chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, from Abu Ja’far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), both said:

The one who buys a slave girl who has a husband for her, so her sale is her divorce. So, if the buyer so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he leaves them both upon their marriage.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect on a slave girl's marriage when she is sold?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the juristic principle that selling a female slave who has a husband automatically effects her divorce (talaq), a ruling derived from the change in ownership affecting the marital bond. It grants the new owner the discretion (ikhtiyar) to either maintain the couple's existing marriage or separate them, reflecting the flexibility in early Shia fiqh regarding the status of slaves' families. This mechanism highlights the interplay between property rights and personal status law in the classical era.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said:

‘The one who buys a slave girl who has a husband for her, so her sale is her divorce. So, if the buyer so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he leaves them both upon their marriage’.
